transcript.customer: Can you search for a matte botanical fabric with cotton, in muted olive?

advice.text:
I searched for a matte botanical fabric containing cotton in muted olive, but the retail search returned no matches. The descriptive fabric index is also unavailable, so I can’t verify a suitable fabric just now; that doesn’t mean one doesn’t exist.

Your direction is lovely: a softened olive botanical on a warm ivory or flax ground could feel natural without becoming stark. I’d favour a softly spaced leaf design and a low-sheen cotton or cotton-blend cloth; cotton content alone doesn’t guarantee a matte finish. A tonal olive botanical would be a quieter alternative.

Would you prefer an olive background, or olive leaves on a lighter ground?

transcript.customer: Does finding a Fabric Master record mean I can buy it?

advice.text:
No — finding a Fabric Master record doesn’t mean the fabric is available to buy. It can confirm an identity or provide design information, but it may include unpublished or unverified fabrics.

A fabric needs to appear in the approved retail results before I can offer it as a purchase option; even then, that doesn’t confirm current stock or price.

For your matte, muted-olive botanical containing cotton, the earlier approved retail search returned no matches, and the descriptive knowledge index was unavailable. So we haven’t verified a purchasable option yet.

transcript.customer: Could you show approved Shambala fabrics instead?

advice.text:
Yes — I found three approved retail Shambala fabrics by Prestigious Textiles: Amber, Jonquil and Lagoon, all from the Parade Collection.

Each contains 8% cotton and 92% polyester, with a vertical pattern repeat of 41.5 cm. They meet your request for some cotton content, but the returned information doesn’t verify a matte finish, botanical motif or muted-olive colouring, so I wouldn’t present them as confirmed matches to your original brief.

You can explore the three verified fabric cards here; current price and availability need checking in the product journey. Would you like to keep muted olive as the priority, or explore these Shambala colourways instead?
